text:
Beatrice: Heads-up team — Q4 hosted API capacity planning. I put together a straw target of +120 A100-class GPUs (US + EU split) to cover a ~40% buffer for expected seasonal traffic. Need buy vs short-term lease recommendations + regional constraints. Any immediate red flags? :thinking_face:

Noah: Quick back-of-envelope on demand vs that 120 number — seems small given our growth curve. Using the Nov peak forecast from last week's telemetry: extra workload ~10k GPU-hours/day.

Noah: Calc I ran:```
forecast_extra_gpu_hours_per_day = 10000
forecast_extra_gpu_hours_per_month = forecast_extra_gpu_hours_per_day * 30  # = 300000
hours_per_gpu_per_month = 24 * 30  # = 720
required_gpus = ceil(forecast_extra_gpu_hours_per_month / hours_per_gpu_per_month)  # = 417 GPUs
```

Noah: So 120 buys buys us ~120 * 720 = 86.4k GPU-hours/mo, which only covers ~29% of the extra hours. We need to reconcile assumptions (are we expecting >1 GPU per request due to batching/kv cache reductions?).

Katie: Finance note — two quick scenarios: buy CAPEX and 36mo depreciation vs lease/OPEX. Rough numbers (ballpark):
- Buy: $24k/GPU upfront (hardware + racks/embedding infra amortized) -> $2.88M for 120 units. Depreciated over 36mo => ~80k/mo.
- Lease/reserved pool: ~$2,200/GPU/month -> 120 units = $264k/mo.
- Burst (short-term spot/lease): ~$3,800/GPU/month (higher) but no capex.

Katie: If we actually need ~420 GPUs, buy is ~10M one-time (practical capex hit). Lease for 420 GPUs =~924k/mo. Need to choose based on expected permanence of demand.

Arjun: Procurement / lead time: vendors said lead time for new chassis with A100-style cards is 8–12 weeks min, likely 10–14 including rack/networking + compliance. Lease pools (partners) can spin up in 2–4 weeks depending on region. For EU there are capacity constraints in Nov — priority slots fill fast.

Arjun: Vendors: AlphaHardware quoted "best-effort" bulk discount at orders >200, but requires 60% deposit and 12wk lead. BetaCloud (managed dedicated) has reserved nodes in US-West by contract in ~3 weeks; EU is thin.

Maya: Ops notes — even with extra hardware we need autoscale tuning + smarter batching and prefix caching to reduce effective GPU-hours. Options: 1) aggressive caching + smaller models for low-priority traffic, 2) adaptive batching window expansion during mild load to improve throughput, 3) regional routing: route EU-critical customers to EU reserved, low-priority to US.

Maya: Also recommend we gate buys to committed enterprise demand — if a customer signs for Dedicated, we can reserve some of the new boxes for them and amortize. For hosted slack bursts, prefer short-term lease + optimizer changes.

Noah: Agree. If we assume we can reduce peak extra hours by ~50% through caching/quantization (optimistic), required GPUs -> ~200. Still larger than 120. So mixed approach: procure 120 owned (long-term base), lease 100–150 for Q4 peak, and reserve burst budget for spot on cloud for unpredictable spikes.

Katie: From finance perspective that hybrid is easiest: smaller capex, predictable baseline cost, and flexible opex for spikes. Need approval for ~$3M capex if we buy 120 units (one-time) + commit ~400–700k/mo opex for leased units during Q4. I'll draft numbers for exec review.

Arjun: Action items: I can start RFP with AlphaHardware + BetaCloud today, ask for EU availability windows and breakouts for 120 vs 200 orders. ETA for quotes 5 business days.

Beatrice: Thanks. Quick decisions checklist:
- Approve RFP (Arjun) -> yes
- Approve provisional capex ask for 120 units -> pending exec review (Katie)
- Plan for 100–150 leased GPUs in US + 40–80 EU for Nov peak -> ops to finalize (Maya/Noah)

deploy-bot: [monitoring] autoscaler notice: average queue length up 22% in hosted-us-west over last 10m, scaling policy triggered additional pods.

Noah: I'll add a short simulation in the capacity playbook with three scenarios (conservative/likely/optimistic) and include model-level ops knobs. Will share by EOD.

Beatrice: Perfect — let's reconvene next Tue after the vendor quotes and Noah's sim. Tagging @Katie for finance review and @Arjun for procurement timeline. :calendar:

Maya: FYI I'll prepare a small runbook for degrading gracefully (route to smaller models + token-rate caps) so SLO stays intact if we underprovision.

Beatrice: Great work everyone.
